title: Static documents and early web scripting context
learningObjectives: Explain static documents and early web scripting context and describe JavaScript's role in web development.

understand.concept: The early web focused on linked documents that browsers retrieved and displayed. As websites evolved into interactive applications, scripting enabled dynamic responses, client-side checks, menus, and richer user interfaces. Server-side code continued to handle trusted data and processing.
understand.whyItMatters: The web's evolution helps explain why JavaScript runs in browsers and why client-side interaction does not replace server responsibilities.
understand.analogy: A static document is like a printed page; a scripted page can respond to the reader's actions.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; language standards and host runtime APIs have precise technical boundaries.

explain.narrative: The HTML document provides the initial content; JavaScript changes the message after a user action.

examples.code: This page starts as a document.
examples.explanation: The HTML document provides the initial content; JavaScript changes the message after a user action.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser page displays or updates text using JavaScript.

questions.prompt: What did browser scripting make possible beyond static document display?
questions.explanation: Scripting enabled interactive behaviour within web pages.

questions.prompt: What should you identify before using a JavaScript API?
questions.explanation: Available APIs depend on whether code runs in a browser, server runtime, or another host.
